newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen up slightly on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen up slightly on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell after a three-session rise and analysts said the strong buying after price-fixing signalled a rebound on Wednesday.
But they said the lower turnover and relatively low volume of the buying after price fixing signalled only slight growth.
"The buying after price-fixing for some stocks seems cosmetic because the volume was so low," said Stanislaw Kutkowski of Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.
Analysts said the news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery ended successfully could help ensure a gain on Wednesday.

But they said the lower house of parliament's surprise tax cut for low earners last month, seen as inflationary, could continue to dampen demand. The Senate, which votes on the bill next week, might oppose the cut, analysts said.
"Especially foreign investors don't like it when the tax situation is unclear," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.5 percent to 13,472.6 points and turnover fell 30.8 percent to 77.5 million zlotys on both markets. Analysts said the market would likely stay above 13,000 points this week.
Analysts were surprised that Debica, which dropped 4.4 percent in active trade, continued to slip after falling 8.1 percent last week.
They said Animex, down four percent, fell in profit-taking after last week's rise buoyed in part by a buy recommendation from Bank Handlowy SA brokerage.

Analysts said Zywiec and BRE, up 3.1 percent and 2.3 percent, were rebounding after significant falls during the market's 14.6-percent drop over much of last month. NFI units fell 3.1 percent to 139.5 million zlotys. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
